items.title: F78's trait defaults make a STAGE-HEAVY program dearer to check: `example:reactive-ui` +4.71% instructions at that one commit, while `example:browser` got 6.14% cheaper, `example:todo` 0.86% and kolt 0.31%
items.body: Measured per commit across reactive-46, every compiler built with one codegen unit, each on its own examples, all checks exit 0. At 0df43a2d: reactive-ui 2,447M -> 2,563M (+4.71%), browser 1,553M -> 1,458M (-6.14%), todo 6,061M -> 6,009M (-0.86%). The change removed 26 hand-written `on_change`/`sub` copies (less std to analyze - the saving every program gets) and made them defaults on `Flow`, which are instantiated per pipe STAGE TYPE the program uses - so a program with many distinct stage types pays per type what the copies cost once. Find where: the default's body is re-inferred or re-selected per instance (M111's disease), or its instantiation mints slots nothing shares (M118's). Acceptance: reactive-ui back at or under its pre-F78 count with the defaults kept; no golden moves.

items.discussion: A152 (reactive-46 699a140f: `zip_some`, `when_all_some`, `unzip`), A150 (bf53a4f4: `states()`, `TransientState::map/zip/and_then`); M103 (Order 45: maps-45's std growth regressed every check), M36 (the base cache is per process), store-46's `store_core` split (the same tax, +9% on a browser example before the split, +1% after); tables under `sweeps/order46/`
items.title: every web program pays for std it does not use: A152's three combinators cost +1.5–1.8% on every measured web example, and A150's `states()` +1.42% on the rpc example - a program that calls none of them
items.body: Per-commit measurement (one codegen unit, own examples, exit 0): at A152, reactive-ui +1.62%, todo +1.51%, browser +1.80%; at A150, todo +1.42%, the others flat. Neither example uses the new surface. std's modules are analyzed whole for every program that loads them, and the web prelude loads most of the reactive family; each order's additions are therefore a flat tax on every check (M103 was the same shape, and store-46 had to split `store_core` out to avoid it). Doors: (a) analyze a std item's BODY only when the program reaches it (signatures always); (b) a persistent, cross-process cache of std's analysis (M36's direction; the incremental paper's 'on-disk world'), so std is analyzed once per toolchain, not once per `vilan check`; (c) keep splitting modules by hand. (b) is the structural answer and fits incremental-analysis.md's records. Until then every std lane reports its delta on the gate's subjects against its own base (Order 47's mechanics should say so). Acceptance: adding an unused std function moves no example's count.
